reference_answer: RelayView verifies owner authority before merge admission. PullRequestMergeStore.admit transactionally inserts a pending effect keyed by binding ID, native PR ID and head revision; an existing identical intent is reused and a conflicting one errors. Only a newly admitted intent dispatches requestExactMerge, fast-forward-only. A provider timeout marks the effect unknown. On retry the coordinator reads provider state and confirms only an observed merged PR with matching head and merged revision; otherwise it leaves the result unknown and throws rather than dispatching again. A concurrent admission that wins the same candidate also prevents a second dispatch. Tests exercise timeout, retry, later observed confirmation and concurrent admission; they do not prove provider-side exactly-once execution or external state after an unreadable provider response.

facts: Merge coordinator uses durable pending/unknown/confirmed effect state.
Store has candidate identity on binding ID, native PR ID, head revision and rejects mismatched intent.
Tests assert one provider merge dispatch across uncertain retries and zero dispatch after concurrent admission.

ambiguities: Read-only observation cannot prove a timed-out provider call did nothing.
Tests use an in-memory SQLite store and fake provider, so they establish local behavior under tested conditions rather than all production races.

must_check: Authority check and durable intent before dispatch
No second dispatch after timeout or concurrent admission
Limits of test and provider guarantees
acceptable_alternatives: A concise state transition description is sufficient if it captures pending, unknown and confirmed.
do_not_penalize: Not specifying the storage table name when the uniqueness key and behavior are correct.

decision_changing_errors: Claiming a timeout is safe to retry by issuing another provider merge.
Claiming the tests establish provider-side exactly-once semantics.
